question: m10
q: Is the Friday dip as big for suburban morning commuters as it is for the CBD?

transcript.answer:
Yes. On this data the Friday dip is as big in the suburbs as in the CBD, and slightly bigger. The two measures aren't identical, though.

| | Pre-COVID (Jan–Mar 2020) | Last 12 months | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Sydney CBD**, Friday 3–7pm tap-ons vs Tue–Thu | 0.905 | about 0.775 (my average of the monthly figures, Oct 2025 – Sep 2026) | about −0.13 |
| **Suburban**, Friday 7–9am tap-ons vs Tue–Thu, all modes | 0.933 | 0.758 | −0.175 |
| **Suburban**, bus only | 0.941 | 0.799 | −0.142 |

- **Level:** Friday volume is now about 76% of a Tue–Thu day in the suburbs (all modes) and about 78% in the CBD. That is roughly the same gap.
- **Change from 2020:** The suburbs have dropped more. Their Friday ratio is down about 17.5 points, against about 13 points for the CBD. In relative terms that is roughly a 19% fall versus 14%.
- **Starting point:** Suburbs were already close to flat across the week before COVID, at 0.93. The CBD already had a modest Friday dip at 0.905. So the suburbs have moved further from where they started.
- **Recent CBD trend:** The CBD ratio has been stable at about 0.74–0.80 since early 2023. The latest month, September 2026, is 0.783.

**Caveats:**
- The measures differ in timing and direction. The CBD figure counts evening exits (3–7pm). The suburban figure counts morning departures from home (7–9am), in everywhere outside the named centres.
- The suburban data is only a single pre-COVID figure and a single last-12-months figure. There is no monthly series, so I can't show its trend.
- The CBD data may not include Sydney Metro taps. That affects levels more than the Friday ratios.
